decision: Publish an explicit, very-low-confidence decision estimate of approximately $4.9 million per 10 QALYs. The model divides Five Keys' $16,667 gross historical expense per ADA-equivalent year by a modeled 10% additional-credential probability and 0.34 QALY per additional credential, then multiplies by 10 QALYs. The 0.34-QALY midpoint applies an 80% transfer and causal discount to a peer-reviewed U.S. model's 1.7 discounted lifetime QALYs per additional high-school graduate. The source model is old and largely association-based; Five Keys serves older, justice-affected learners and includes equivalency credentials, so this is a judgmental donor estimate rather than a measured Five Keys health effect. The joint positive-effect sensitivity is approximately $490,000 to $66.7 million, and a true null remains plausible.

sourceEvidence.nearestEvidence: A peer-reviewed U.S. cost-utility model of class-size reduction and high-school graduation
sourceEvidence.studyPopulation: U.S. students modeled from Project STAR education effects and national education-health data

fiveKeysQalyPerAdditionalCredential.basis: The midpoint retains 20% of the published 1.7-QALY estimate: an explicit 80% discount for residual confounding, a 2007 model and mortality assumptions, adult and justice-affected learner transfer, diploma-versus-equivalency differences, and uncertain persistence. The 0.05-1.7 range is a decision range, not a confidence interval.

sourceEvidence.boundary: The paper modeled lifetime health gains associated with producing an additional high-school graduate through smaller elementary-school classes. It did not study Five Keys, adult education, custody settings, GED/HiSET pathways, or philanthropy. Its education-health coefficients do not establish that Five Keys causes 1.7 QALYs per credential.

additionalCredentialProbabilityPerAdaYea.basis: Existing MFI decision scenarios; Five Keys has not measured its causal credential effect.

sensitivity.case: Published health model; central credential effect

modeledBridge.nullBoundary: The numeric range is conditional on two positive effects: Five Keys must cause additional credentials, and those credentials must cause additional lifetime health utility. Neither is measured for Five Keys. If either effect is zero, or a private gift displaces public funding rather than adding instruction, the impact price has no finite upper bound.

excludedBenefits: Employment, earnings, housing, public safety, family, and community spillovers
Government medical, custody, or social-service savings
Any benefit from education short of causing an additional credential
